title: fix: chats stay queued after restoring obsolete child completions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes chats remaining “Waiting for turn to start” after a Gateway restart restores a completion batch whose child executions have been superseded.

## User Impact

New messages can start without being parked indefinitely behind an obsolete, unprepared completion reservation. A mixed batch can still deliver its current children's findings, and cancelled children that have not been superseded still report their outcome.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restoration could reserve the full frozen completion cohort, while live preparation used the filtered findings list to revalidate that same cohort. An obsolete member made preparation return before adopting the reservation, leaving later inputs blocked in FIFO even with no active execution.

Use the existing current-cohort predicate before reserving wholly obsolete batches. Keep full-cohort identity and durable outcome custody separate from findings selection, quietly complete batches with no eligible findings, and recheck selected findings before effects. The existing completion-finalization composition moves into the adjacent state module to keep the dispatcher within its existing size limit.

Messaging policy, execution authority, schemas, and stored formats are unchanged. This is a follow-up bug fix to the lifecycle consolidation merged in #177698, independent of the outstanding policy proposals.

## Evidence

### Consumer-test repair at `1b361a0b53d6d06d3a974d41a4f2e6db06c8679e`

The two review findings and all three reported CI assertions are repaired. The mailbox fixture now distinguishes cancellation from supersession: cancelled yielded work still reserves its owed report, while superseded work before or during requester lookup permits the real foreground mailbox claim. The mixed-child route-notice case now requires one delivery from the current siblings even when its triggering child is obsolete, excludes the obsolete output, and retains the sorted 1,024-character notice bound.

Before this repair, the unchanged reviewed head `1e346af8b9602b1244da9c23c74100b35650a909` reproduced the two mailbox failures and the requester-wake failure locally. Afterward, **63 tests pass across the mailbox, requester-wake and requester-dispatch suites** (23.94 seconds wrapper wall time across two shards). The mailbox table adds four explicit supersession cases; no assertions, cancellation guarantees, timeouts or baselines are weakened.

Owning agent-session test types, scoped typed lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass. Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the complete test repair with the unchanged production owners found no actionable findings. This commit changes only two test files; the existing built-Gateway restart proof below remains evidence for the identical production patch. New-head hosted CI is pending, not claimed green.

### Original production repair and runtime evidence

- Synthetic regressions on base `52df852cd5be`: the obsolete reservation and mixed-cohort cases fail for the reported reasons; the current-cancelled-child control passes.
- Original production candidate `1e346af8b960`: 87 tests pass across requester dispatch, restart, cancellation, ownership, and durable requester-wake settlement. The added preparation race rejects findings that become superseded before execution or storage effects.
- Original focused test command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.requester-settle-dispatch.test.ts src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.requester-settle-restart.test.ts src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.requester-settle-cancel.test.ts src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.requester-settle-ownership.test.ts src/agents/subagents/completion/subagent-completion-admission.requester-wake.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 55.86 seconds wall time across two shards; the changed dispatch file's standalone run took 10.01 seconds wall time, about 0.3 seconds executing tests. CI timing is not yet available.
- The full production build, targeted agent/session typechecking, lint, and formatting pass. Independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

An isolated built Gateway also passed the restart flow using a scripted loopback model provider (not a real-provider qualification):

```text
public sessions.create: requester and two children created
fixture Gateway: stopped and joined
canonical offline fixture writer: 2 terminal, suppressed, superseded child rows
restored wake: dispatching yielded cohort, attemptCount=1, rearmGeneration=1
same-profile Gateway restart: registryActivationRuns=2, active=0, recovered=0, success
public chat.send: started
agent.wait: ok
persisted assistant reply: present, same requester incarnation
obsolete child findings injected: false
all owned fixture processes: stopped and joined
```

The captured build contains this working patch on base `52df852cd5be`; focused tests above cover mixed-cohort delivery and supersession during preparation. No claim of authenticated external-provider or browser testing is made. The build exited successfully but reported a UI startup bundle budget warning (318.1 KiB versus 318.0 KiB); this patch changes no UI files.

Related symptom reports: #143334 and #158154. Their root causes have not been established as identical, so this PR does not claim to close them.

All regression fixtures are synthetic. No private transcripts, session identifiers, hostnames, endpoints, or credentials are included.


Related follow-up: #180728 repairs independently admitted child executions being rejected by an in-process facade after their recovered parent finishes. This PR instead repairs obsolete completion reservations blocking admission before an execution starts. The fixes are independent and complement the merged lifecycle consolidation #177698; neither changes messaging or authority policy.
